items.title: fix(aggregator): attention never serves fixtures in live mode (#1116)
items.body: ## The defect (#1116) On 2026-11-10 the production attention feed served the bundled demo fixtures for ~10 minutes. Chain of causes, all verified on the wire: 1. The OpenCode prod server restarted repeatedly during fleet work (7 starts 14:33–15:03 CST, one exit status 130). 2. Two fleet-feed collector runs (14:53:37, 14:58:27 CST) could not reach it — journal: `collector: OpenCode server unreachable; attention empty` — and, behaving as written, published a feed with `attention: []` and exited 0. 3. The aggregator's direct laptop leg had been **silently dead since 2026-10-29**: it reads port+password from the OpenChamber-managed server's state file, which still names a dead pid/port. Sessions actually live on the standing `opencode.service` (127.0.0.1:13420). Attention was single-legged and nobody could see it. 4. With zero merged entries, live `attention()` fell into its designed fallback and returned `FIXTURE_ATTENTION` — synthetic session IDs that 404 on the real server, with timestamps regenerated at read time so they look fresh. The feed self-recovered when the collector's 15:03:40 CST run landed (60 sessions) — **no aggregator restart was involved**; the flip and flip-back are both explained by the per-request fallback engaging/disengaging. `/api/quota.json` was never affected (verified: API and quota-current.json agree, all pools freshly measured). ## The fix - **`src/sources/live.ts`** — the empty-attention branch now returns `[]` with provenance `unavailable (no live attention source reachable; fixtures withheld in live mode)` plus a logged error. Production attention never serves fixtures again. - **`src/sources/live.ts` + `src/config.ts`** — `laptopMapped()` reads the standing server first (`~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`, new `PM_AGG_OPENCODE_SERVER_STATE` / `opencodeServerStateFile`), OpenChamber-managed as leg 2. Per-leg health is tracked and named in the attention provenance (`[laptop legs: openchamber leg down]`) instead of failing silently. - **`scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts`** — a failed server read carries the last-good attention entries (`attention-last-good.json`, same pattern as `aa-last-good.json`) and still marks the section `error`; a fresh successful read refreshes the file. One bad read can no longer zero the feed. - **`test/attention-no-fixtures-1116.test.ts`** — the incident shape end-to-end: empty feed + dead legs → empty list, `unavailable` provenance, zero fixture IDs; standing-server leg serving real sessions with an empty feed; non-empty feed pass-through. ## Verification - New tests: 3/3 pass. Adjacent suites (charges-feed-gate, attention-classification, config): 19/19. Typecheck clean for the touched files. - Full aggregator suite: 1,893 pass / 22 fail in the worktree vs 1,861 pass / 18 fail on unmodified main in the same environment — the named failures are identical pre-existing ones (boot-test hook timeouts under load, pass-through pool assembly, inFlightBoardItems, collector projects parsing, renderProgramProject). - Post-deploy wire proof to be appended here after the aggregator redeploys from main. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(usage-hub): overview stale-feed warning + drill rendered-page evidence (#1116 item 5)
items.body: Queue task 14246 — closes the item (5) acceptance gap for #1116 (does not close #1116; stewardship item (4) is out of scope and separate). ## Problem The drill verified feed age in `/api/health` but nothing asserted the rendered dashboard visibly warns after collector failure. The overview Health strip said 'feed X old' — not an actionable warning. ## Change - `src/render.ts` (`renderOverviewBody`): when `feedAgeMs >= FEED_STALE_MS`, render an explicit `Feed stale — last collection … ago … Check health` banner (`data-signal="feed-stale"` hook). Unknown age never warns. - `scripts/age-feed-drill.sh`: after the health signal fires, fetch the overview page (new `PM_DRILL_PAGE_CMD` knob, default local curl) and record `page_warn_seen` (true/false/null-unknown) in the result JSON. Best effort — pass criteria (signal + restore) unchanged. - Tests: new `test/overview-stale-feed-1116.test.ts` (deterministic render assertions: past/at-threshold warn, fresh/unknown silent); `test/age-feed-drill.test.ts` gains a page plan (warn/silent/fail) + 3 tests. `bash -n` clean. - Targeted: 33 pass / 0 fail across the 3 files (rebased on current origin/main, re-run post-rebase). ## Evidence for the live drill The scheduled interlocked drill now produces both halves of the acceptance evidence on each run: the `/api/health` payload (existing) and `page_warn_seen` for the rendered warning (new), in `age-feed-result.json`, without touching interlocks, lock, or restoration. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): stop printing "old old" after ageMsText ages
items.body: Found by the 2026-11-23 PM pages review (live screenshot pass over every PM stack page). `ageMsText()` already returns `"2m old"` / `"1.5h old"` / `"fresh"`, but seven call sites appended a second `" old"`: - `src/render.ts` — the Overview health strip rendered **"feed 2m old old"** (and "feed fresh old" in the first 90 s). - `src/watchdog.ts` — six watchdog alert strings (orchestration stale, registry stale, Project #4 audit, host-health snapshot) read "…5m old old…" in the alert pushes. Fix: drop the redundant suffix at every site. No test asserted the doubled strings (checked `watchdog.test.ts`, `overview-stale-feed-1116.test.ts`). Diff is exactly 7 one-line string edits across 2 files. Note: the live dashboard is built from a 2026-11-15 commit, so this becomes visible only when the pm-aggregator deployment next follows main — that gap is the review's headline finding and is filed separately. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(usage-hub): report pm-feed collector checkout drift in health (#1116 item 3)
items.body: Implements item (3) of #1116 (queue task 3010): the pm-feed checkout drift check. Items (1)/(2) landed via #1138/#1148/#1151 and are not rebuilt; item (4) (stewardship naming) and the item (5) acceptance verification are split into a follow-up queue task — see below. ## What changed - **New `pm-stack/aggregator/src/checkout-drift.ts`** — `computeCheckoutDrift(cwd, run?)` measures the collector checkout's HEAD vs its `origin/main` ref (rev-parse + rev-list counts, injectable git runner). States follow the health view's honesty rules: `in-sync` (behindBy 0), `behind` (exact count), or `unknown` **with a reason** (git unreadable, count failure, or local commits not on origin/main). It never fetches — collection must not mutate the checkout it runs from — so a stale ref understates rather than invents drift, and both SHAs are reported. - **Collector** (`scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts`) embeds the result as `feed.checkout` every run, fail-soft. - **`feed.ts`** — `FleetFeed.checkout?: CheckoutDrift` (absent in older feeds). - **`health.ts`** — `/api/health` and `/health` surface `feed.checkout` verbatim; a feed with no report surfaces `unknown` with the reason "collector did not report checkout drift (feed predates the #1116 drift check)" instead of silence. `behind` marks the view degraded. - **`render.ts`** — the health page's collector card names the drift: behind-by-N badge, in-sync, or unknown-with-reason. ## Tests (laptop, bun) - New `test/checkout-drift.test.ts` (7 tests): in-sync, behind-by-N, unreadable checkout → unknown, local commits → unknown, plus buildHealth surfacing (absent → unknown-with-reason; behind → verbatim + degraded; in-sync → not degraded). - `bun test test/checkout-drift.test.ts test/health.test.ts` — 23 pass. `test/render.test.ts test/feed.test.ts test/boot.test.ts` — 39 pass. - `tsc --noEmit` could not run in the fresh worktree (bun type definitions not installed there); CI is the typecheck of record. ## Not in this PR - Item (4): the stewardship skill files (SKILL.md/CHARTER.md/COMMISSION.md) contain no stale-feed naming and no DAILY CONSOLE READS block was found in them this shift; the live hourly instructions still need verifying and, if absent, the naming added there. - Item (5): the acceptance harness exists (kill-collector-drill, #1283) and the stale-feed surfacing is covered by health tests, but the end-to-end footer-prominence check was not re-run this shift. Refs #1116 (does not close it — items 4/5 remain). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: test(id-web): softbreak marked-span round-trip regression tests (#981)
items.body: ## What Adds the #981 regression tests to `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`: - `test_softbreak_marked_span_roundtrip_fixpoint` — strong/em/strikethrough spans crossing a soft line break save as the normalized single-line form, are a fixpoint on the second save, and contain no ` ` entities. - `test_softbreak_link_roundtrip_fixpoint` — a link whose text crosses a soft break stays one link on save, with and without a title. Tests only; no production code change. ## Why Triage (queue task 1132) found the #981 corruption is already fixed on current main: the packet's probe (2026-10-26T15:18Z, main 24261355) predates PR #999 (merged 18:28Z), whose `append_inline_child` merging (commit d3e7c548) also merges the marked `" "` node the SoftBreak arm emits and identical link wrappers. Verified on current main with the standalone verbatim-codec probe — all packet cases round-trip to the normalized single-line form, fixpoint, no entities (logs: goal hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1510-t1116/crate/out3.log). These tests lock that incidental fix in so a future mark-chain change cannot silently re-break softbreak spans. ## Verification - Behavior asserted by the tests was verified case-by-case with the standalone codec probe on current main (same inputs, byte-exact expected outputs). - Full `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown` was not run in the sandbox: the crate's test build needs the `web/dist` prerequisite and OOM'd there earlier today (recorded in task 1116's park reason). PR CI is the test runner for this change. Closes #981 once merged (the fix itself landed in #999; this PR adds its missing regression coverage). --- Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id-web): html_inline passthrough — inline HTML round-trips unescaped (#943)
items.body: Fixes #943 — queue task 1131 (representation decided by triage task 1090). **Problem:** `markdown_to_prosemirror` converted non-img `HtmlInline` nodes to plain text nodes, and the save-direction comrak text renderer backslash-escapes angle brackets — opening and saving a file rewrote every inline HTML tag (``, ``, ``, …) as literal escaped text. **Change:** - `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` (parse): the `HtmlInline` arm now emits an `html_inline` atom node carrying the raw tag in `attrs.html` (img / linked-img handling unchanged — checked first, as before). - `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` (save): `json_to_ast` gains an `html_inline` case returning `NodeValue::HtmlInline(tag)`, which comrak renders verbatim (same precedent as sized images). Full passthrough — no tag whitelist. - `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts`: `richSchema` gains the `html_inline` atom node spec. Its `toDOM` renders the tag as inert text in a `span[data-html-inline]` — the `html` attr is never rendered via `innerHTML` or as live markup. - Tests: new `web::markdown` unit tests — sub/sup/u round-trip unescaped + fixpoint, the parse shape (open/close tags as two `html_inline` nodes), and generality (``, ``). **Verified:** editor.ts transpiles clean (bun build). Local `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown` did not complete in the worker shift — the sandbox lib-test compile repeatedly stalls/OOMs (same environment limitation recorded for task 1116) — so the new Rust tests are verified by this PR's CI; the task is parked awaiting it and merges on green. Queue task 1131. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Inline HTML tags in Markdown are now preserved when content is parsed, edited, and saved, instead of being converted to marked text or escaped during serialization. * In the editor, inline HTML is displayed as inert text rather than rendered as live markup.

items.title: refactor: remove the remaining Supabase code paths; Turso is the only remote store
items.body: Before: the Supabase project (muse-dev2) is deleted and every live service already runs on Turso, but the repo still carried code that could reach Supabase. That included a selectable `supabase` backend in the aggregator and the queue broker, a quota exporter for the deleted project, backup paths and options, a disabled mirror module, and Postgres-only helper scripts. Setting the wrong env var would point a service back at a host that no longer exists. After: nothing in the repo can talk to Supabase, and Turso is the only remote store. Owner's request: "fix all uses of supabase". ## What changed - **pm-aggregator** - `PM_AGG_STORE_BACKEND` accepts only `file` or `turso`. - `src/supabase.ts` is deleted. The SQL helpers moved to `src/sql-client.ts`, and the remote stores are renamed for Turso. The SQL itself is unchanged. - Removed the Supabase usage-export overlay and `scripts/migrate-stores-to-supabase.ts`. - `install.sh` now writes `PM_AGG_STORE_BACKEND=turso`. It used to write `supabase`, which would have failed at startup. - **pm-stack/supabase-export**: removed, together with its CI step and test-registry entry. - **fleet-queue** - The queue broker is Turso-only. Leaving `QUEUE_BROKER_BACKEND` unset means turso; any other value exits 3. The deployed unit already sets `turso`. - Deleted `supabase-exec.py`. - **Backups** - Removed the laptop-backups `supabase` option, the disabled `supabase-turso-coord-mirror` module, the Supabase export in `pm-dashboard-backup.sh` (its opt-out is renamed `PM_AGG_STORE_EXPORT`), cold-store's `backup-supabase`, and agent-backup's Postgres-only scripts. - **Comments**: stale Supabase comments elsewhere are trimmed to describe current state. ## Kept on purpose - The R2 bucket name `supabase-backups`, because live backups still write there. Renaming it is an infrastructure change. - Supabase as a plain vendor name in the aggregator's SaaS and charges data. - Dated docs, SQL migrations, and the job ids in `prune_m1.sql`'s keep-list. - The `supabase.muse-dev2.*` entries in `secrets/sops/common/bws.yaml`. Removing them is a secrets change and is left for the owner. ## Tests | Suite | Command | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | aggregator | `cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test` | 2997 pass | 2974 pass, 0 fail | | aggregator typecheck | `bunx tsc --noEmit` | — | clean | | dispatch | `cd pm-stack/dispatch && bun test` | — | 230 pass | | fleet-queue / fleet-secrets | `cargo test -p fleet-queue -p fleet-secrets --all-features` | 447 / 29 | 445 / 29, all pass | | cold-store-reaper | `pytest` | 206 pass | 202 pass | | agent-backup | `pytest` | — | 2 pass | | agent-backup | `test-backup.sh` | — | PASS | - **Aggregator:** the 23 fewer tests are exactly the removed Supabase-only tests, net of the ones added. - **fleet-queue:** the 2 fewer tests are the removed Supabase-only tests. - **cold-store-reaper:** 5 Supabase-only tests removed, 1 added. - **`nixos/home/*.test.sh`:** the manifest test now passes. The copy test still has the same 4 failures it had before this change; they come from running as root. - **Other checks:** `bash -n` and `nix-instantiate --parse` pass on every shell and Nix file touched. ## Checked live On the laptop, `pm-aggregator` and `pm-dashboard-backup` already run with `PM_AGG_STORE_BACKEND=turso`. The user journal shows no service reaching Supabase since the 2026-11-20 dispatch restart. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? ### Compress/s2: Integer Overflow or Wraparound and Out-of-bounds Write in compress
[CVE-2026-63209](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63209) / [GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Signed Integer Overflow in s2.NewDict

##### Summary

A signed integer overflow vulnerability in `s2.NewDict()` allows an attacker to bypass repeat index validation by supplying a dictionary with a uvarint-encoded repeat value exceeding `MaxInt64`. When `Dict.Encode()` is subsequently called, the overflowed negative repeat value causes an out-of-bounds memory access via `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic, crashing the process with SIGSEGV.

##### Package

- **Name:** `github.com/klauspost/compress/s2`
- **Ecosystem:** Go
- **Affected versions:** <= v1.18.6 (all versions with `NewDict` function)

##### Severity

**High (7.5)** — CVSS v3.1: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

##### Vulnerability

##### Type
- CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write (via unsafe.Pointer)

##### Description

The `NewDict()` function reads a uvarint from dictionary data and converts it to `int`:

```go
r, n := binary.Uvarint(dict)
// ...
d.repeat = int(r)
if d.repeat > len(dict) {
    return nil
}
```

When `r` exceeds `MaxInt64` (9223372036854775807), `int(r)` overflows to a negative value. Since a negative number is never greater than a positive length, the validation check is bypassed.

When `Dict.Encode()` is called, the negative `repeat` value causes an integer overflow in `encodeBlockDictGo()`:

```go
repeat := len(dict.dict) - dict.repeat  // overflows: 62 - (-5758978476775341977) = huge positive
candidate := len(dict.dict) - repeat + s // underflows to negative
load32(dict.dict, candidate)             // OOB via unsafe.Pointer
```

`load32` calls `le.Load32` which uses `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic without bounds checking:

```go
func Load32[I Indexer](b []byte, i I) uint32 {
    return *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)), i))
}
```

This causes a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) when the negative index is dereferenced.

##### PoC

```go
package main

import (
    "encoding/binary"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/klauspost/compress/s2"
)

func main() {
    var dictData []byte
    buf := make([]byte, binary.MaxVarintLen64)
    n := binary.PutUvarint(buf, 12687765596934209639) // > MaxInt64
    dictData = append(dictData, buf[:n]...)
    dictData = append(dictData, make([]byte, 16)...) // minimum dict size

    dict := s2.NewDict(dictData)
    // dict is non-nil despite invalid repeat value (overflow bypassed validation)

    src := make([]byte, 64)
    for i := range src { src[i] = byte(i) }
    dict.Encode(nil, src) // SIGSEGV: OOB access via unsafe.Pointer
}
```

##### Impact

- **Denial of Service:** The process crashes immediately with SIGSEGV

##### Attack Vector

Any application that:
1. Accepts user-supplied S2 dictionary data via `s2.NewDict()`
2. Calls `Dict.Encode()` on any data ≥32 bytes

##### Suggested Fix

Validate the uvarint value before converting to int:

```go
if r > math.MaxInt64 {
    return nil
}
d.repeat = int(r)
```

Or use `uint` for the repeat field and validate against `uint(len(dict))`.

##### References

- Source: `s2/dict.go` lines 59-61 (vulnerability), `s2/encode_all.go` line 947 (crash site)
- Commit: 539243b (v1.18.6 + 4 commits)
